chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Russell Procope: jolly Fletcher alumnus carrying the kidding into Ellington's band
summary: Procope stayed with Fletcher a long time, was a good reader, and brought Hawkins-style joking into Duke's band.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Yeah. So he stayed down there. But this is what I was told. I never saw this. I still would believe it. But nevertheless Procope was in Fletcher's band, and he, along with Hilton Victor Jefferson -- I think Hawk was in the band then, and Buster Bailey was playing clarinet, and doubling on tenor for parts. And Procope could play, always was fast, and he stayed with Fletcher's band quite a long time. And he toured and everything, and he's another one of those -- he was always a jolly little guy, you know? Did you ever meet him personally?
I've never talked to him. Of course, I've seen him -- with Ellington. Billie.

Well, he was always jolly. And even in Duke's band, when he joined Duke's band, which was his last big band -- he was in Fletcher's band so long with that era, along with Jimmy Harrison, Coleman Hawkins, so he injected stuff in Duke's band too, a lot of that kidding and stuff.
I knew this because when even I went to see Duke two or three places, you know, Procope was carrying on this same stuff, and I said, "uh-huh, here's another Coleman Hawkins."
And he'd laugh. He knew where it came from, see, but he was always jolly, and if he was worried about anything, you never knew

it because he was one of the guys that could hide it real well, but he was an excellent musician, always could read. He was a very good reader, and I really -- I'm happy that we still have him around.
